criteria.criterion: NASA's DART mission changed Dimorphos' orbital period around Didymos by at least 73 seconds
required_elements: NASA defined success as a change of 73 seconds or more in Dimorphos' orbit period
DART actually changed Dimorphos' orbital period around Didymos by at least 73 seconds
criteria.promise_scope: NASA set a mission success threshold for the DART mission: Dimorphos' orbital period around Didymos would change by at least 73 seconds. Beneficiary/location are not human/geographic; the specified object and setting are Dimorphos' orbit around Didymos.
criteria.observed_scope: c2 reports the investigation team confirmed DART's impact altered Dimorphos' orbit around Didymos by 32 minutes, shortening the orbit from 11 hours 55 minutes to 11 hours 23 minutes; c3 further reports the orbital period finally settled at 11 hours 22 minutes and 3 seconds, 33 minutes and 15 seconds less than before impact.

delivery_support.quote: Now, the investigation team has confirmed the spacecraft’s impact altered Dimorphos’ orbit around Didymos by 32 minutes, shortening the 11 hour and 55-minute orbit to 11 hours and 23 minutes.

Over the following weeks, the asteroid’s orbital period continued to shorten as Dimorphos lost more rocky material to space, finally settling at 11 hours, 22 minutes, and 3 seconds per orbit – 33 minutes and 15 seconds less time than before impact.

trace.reasoning:
Requested scope: Did NASA's DART mission meet its target for changing how long Dimorphos takes to orbit Didymos?

NASA's DART mission changed Dimorphos' orbital period around Didymos by at least 73 seconds
Status: DELIVERED
c2 reports the investigation team confirmed DART's impact altered Dimorphos' orbit around Didymos by 32 minutes, shortening the orbit from 11 hours 55 minutes to 11 hours 23 minutes; c3 further reports the orbital period finally settled at 11 hours 22 minutes and 3 seconds, 33 minutes and 15 seconds less than before impact.
Promised scope: NASA set a mission success threshold for the DART mission: Dimorphos' orbital period around Didymos would change by at least 73 seconds. Beneficiary/location are not human/geographic; the specified object and setting are Dimorphos' orbit around Didymos.
Observed scope: c2 reports the investigation team confirmed DART's impact altered Dimorphos' orbit around Didymos by 32 minutes, shortening the orbit from 11 hours 55 minutes to 11 hours 23 minutes; c3 further reports the orbital period finally settled at 11 hours 22 minutes and 3 seconds, 33 minutes and 15 seconds less than before impact.
Supported delivery: c2 reports the investigation team confirmed DART's impact altered Dimorphos' orbit around Didymos by 32 minutes, shortening the orbit from 11 hours 55 minutes to 11 hours 23 minutes; c3 further reports the orbital period finally settled at 11 hours 22 minutes and 3 seconds, 33 minutes and 15 seconds less than before impact.
Promise evidence: c1
Delivery evidence: c2, c3

Cited source excerpts (promise, delivery, or context as assessed above):
c1: “Before its encounter, NASA had defined a minimum successful orbit period change of Dimorphos as change of 73 seconds or more.”
https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-confirms-dart-mission-impact-changed-asteroids-motion-in-space/

c2: “Prior to DART’s impact, it took Dimorphos 11 hours and 55 minutes to orbit its larger parent asteroid, Didymos. Since DART’s intentional collision with Dimorphos on Sept. 26, astronomers have been using telescopes on Earth to measure how much that time has changed. Now, the investigation team has confirmed the spacecraft’s impact altered Dimorphos’ orbit around Didymos by 32 minutes, shortening the 11 hour and 55-minute orbit to 11 hours and 23 minutes. This measurement has a margin of uncertainty of approximately plus or minus 2 minutes.”
https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-confirms-dart-mission-impact-changed-asteroids-motion-in-space/

c3: “Over the following weeks, the asteroid’s orbital period continued to shorten as Dimorphos lost more rocky material to space, finally settling at 11 hours, 22 minutes, and 3 seconds per orbit – 33 minutes and 15 seconds less time than before impact. This calculation is accurate to within 1 1⁄2 seconds, Naidu said.”
https://www.nasa.gov/missions/dart/nasa-study-asteroids-orbit-shape-changed-after-dart-impact/?rand=772114

c4: “After further analysis, NASA confirmed that DART’s hypervelocity impact with Dimorphos successfully altered Dimorphos’ orbit around Didymos, marking humanity’s first time purposely changing the motion of a celestial object and the first demonstration of asteroid deflection technology.”
https://science.nasa.gov/planetary-defense-dart/
